Item.ItemTitle: Unit 4: The Integration Object – Mastering the Ecosystem

Unit.UnitTitle: Unit 4: The Integration Object – Mastering the Ecosystem

Session.Title: 4.1 The Integration Object: Scaling Modular Power

Section.Paragraph: In the previous units, we learned how to define a Blueprint (Unit 2) and freeze it into an Artifact (Unit 3). But real software doesn't live in isolation. Unit 4 introduces the Integration Object—where multiple modular artifacts combine to form a complex, high-stakes system.

Our case study is LNbits, a Bitcoin Lightning Network wallet system. LNbits is inherently modular (built on "extensions"). By applying our Nix/uv foundations, we can build extensions that are perfectly reproducible, even when they rely on complex backends like Bitcoin nodes.
Instead of a single "monolithic" application, we think of the system as a Composition.

NumberedList.ListItem: Foundation: The Nix/uv environment we've mastered.
Backend: The LNbits core (managed as a Nix flake input).
Specialist: Our custom Scrum Extension, which adds project management features to the wallet.

Section.Paragraph: By keeping these objects encapsulated, we can upgrade the LNbits core without breaking our Scrum extension, because their dependencies never "leak" into each other.

Session.Title: 4.3 The Capstone: The Bitcoin-Powered Scrum Board

Section.Paragraph: The final practice object is a Scrum Extension for LNbits. This tool allows a team to:

BulletedList.ListItem: Manage a backlog using the ScrumMD standard.
"Stake" satoshis (Bitcoin) on tasks to represent priority or commitment.
Visualize progress through an integrated board.

Section.Paragraph: Because this is built as an Integration Object, the entire developer environment—including the Bitcoin regtest node—is launched with a single command: nix develop.

Session.Title: 🛠️ The Hands-on Object: Launching the Ecosystem

Section.Paragraph: In this final laboratory, you will not just run a script; you will launch a modular ecosystem.

Section.Title: Step 1: The Integration
Section.Paragraph: We will link our local extension into a running LNbits instance using a unified Nix Flake.

Section.Title: Step 2: The Practical Win
Section.Paragraph: You will move from a "Blank Screen" to a fully functional, Bitcoin-aware development environment in under 60 seconds.

Section.Title: 🧩 Practice Object: The Reproducible Ecosystem
Section.Paragraph: To complete the course, launch the Unit 4 Laboratory.

NumberedList.ListItem: Navigate to the laboratory folder: ou_tm470/oer/lab/unit4_integration/.
Run nix develop to enter the integrated environment.
Launch the LNbits instance and verify the Scrum extension is active.

Section.Paragraph: Reflective Question: Now that you've seen a complex system launched from a single blueprint, how has your view of "installation" changed? Is there any part of this stack that isn't reproducible?

Paragraph.i: Pedagogical Note: Unit 4 represents the "Synthesis" phase of Tait’s framework, where granular concepts are integrated into a meaningful, functional whole.
